title: Minimum Possible Maximum Waiting Time

"""
URL: https://leetcode.com/problems/minimum-possible-maximum-waiting-time/description/?envType=problem-list-v2&envId=vn57k9wr

4009. Minimum Possible Maximum Waiting Time

You are given an integer array demand, where demand[i] is the amount of fuel required by the i-th car.

You are also given an integer array fuel of length 2. There are exactly two fuel dispensers, numbered 0 and 1, where fuel[j] is the initial amount of fuel available in dispenser j.

Cars are allowed to start refueling in increasing index order. Car 0 becomes allowed at time 0, and for each i > 0, car i becomes allowed exactly when car i - 1 starts refueling.

The refueling process follows these rules:

- Each dispenser can serve at most one car at a time.
- When a car becomes allowed, you must choose a dispenser with at least demand[i] fuel remaining. If both dispensers have enough fuel remaining, you may choose either of them, regardless of when they become free.
- The car waits until the chosen dispenser becomes free and starts refueling immediately. It cannot switch dispensers or intentionally wait after the chosen dispenser becomes free.
- When a car starts refueling, the remaining fuel in the chosen dispenser decreases by demand[i], and the dispenser remains occupied for demand[i] seconds.
- Once started, refueling cannot be interrupted.
- If neither dispenser has at least demand[i] fuel remaining when car i becomes allowed, the process terminates and no further cars can be served.

The waiting time of a car is the time between when it becomes allowed to start refueling and when it actually starts.

Return the minimum possible value of the maximum waiting time among all served cars over all assignments that maximize the number of served cars. If no car can be served, return -1.

Example 1:

Input: demand = [6,8,4,6,5], fuel = [16,13]
Output: 6
Explanation:
The following assignment serves all five cars:

Car | Becomes allowed at | Starts refueling at | Dispenser used | Remaining fuel before start (dispenser 0, dispenser 1) | Waiting time
0   | 0                  | 0                   | 0              | (16, 13)                                             | 0
1   | 0                  | 0                   | 1              | (10, 13)                                             | 0
2   | 0                  | 6                   | 0              | (10, 5)                                              | 6
3   | 6                  | 10                  | 0              | (6, 5)                                               | 4
4   | 10                 | 10                  | 1              | (0, 5)                                               | 0

Thus, all five cars are served, and the maximum waiting time is 6.

To serve all five cars, dispenser 0 must serve the cars with demands 6, 4, and 6, while dispenser 1 must serve the cars with demands 8 and 5. Therefore, car 2 must wait until time 6 for dispenser 0 to become free, so no assignment serving all five cars can have a maximum waiting time less than 6.

Example 2:

Input: demand = [10,15], fuel = [12,17]
Output: 0
Explanation:
- At time 0, Car 0 becomes allowed and starts refuelling using dispenser 0.
- Car 1 becomes allowed at time 0 (when Car 0 starts) and immediately starts refuelling using dispenser 1.
- Both cars start without waiting, so the maximum waiting time is 0.

Example 3:

Input: demand = [10,5], fuel = [8,8]
Output: -1
Explanation:
- At time 0, Car 0 becomes allowed. However, neither dispenser has enough fuel to serve it, so the process terminates immediately.
- No car is served, so the answer is -1.

Constraints:

    1 <= demand.length <= 50
    1 <= demand[i] <= 20
    fuel.length == 2
    1 <= fuel[i] <= 50
"""

solution:
"""
URL: https://leetcode.com/problems/minimum-possible-maximum-waiting-time/description/?envType=problem-list-v2&envId=vn57k9wr

4009. Minimum Possible Maximum Waiting Time

You are given an integer array demand, where demand[i] is the amount of fuel required by the i-th car.

You are also given an integer array fuel of length 2. There are exactly two fuel dispensers, numbered 0 and 1, where fuel[j] is the initial amount of fuel available in dispenser j.

Cars are allowed to start refueling in increasing index order. Car 0 becomes allowed at time 0, and for each i > 0, car i becomes allowed exactly when car i - 1 starts refueling.

The refueling process follows these rules:

- Each dispenser can serve at most one car at a time.
- When a car becomes allowed, you must choose a dispenser with at least demand[i] fuel remaining. If both dispensers have enough fuel remaining, you may choose either of them, regardless of when they become free.
- The car waits until the chosen dispenser becomes free and starts refueling immediately. It cannot switch dispensers or intentionally wait after the chosen dispenser becomes free.
- When a car starts refueling, the remaining fuel in the chosen dispenser decreases by demand[i], and the dispenser remains occupied for demand[i] seconds.
- Once started, refueling cannot be interrupted.
- If neither dispenser has at least demand[i] fuel remaining when car i becomes allowed, the process terminates and no further cars can be served.

The waiting time of a car is the time between when it becomes allowed to start refueling and when it actually starts.

Return the minimum possible value of the maximum waiting time among all served cars over all assignments that maximize the number of served cars. If no car can be served, return -1.

Example 1:

Input: demand = [6,8,4,6,5], fuel = [16,13]
Output: 6
Explanation:
The following assignment serves all five cars:

Car | Becomes allowed at | Starts refueling at | Dispenser used | Remaining fuel before start (dispenser 0, dispenser 1) | Waiting time
0   | 0                  | 0                   | 0              | (16, 13)                                             | 0
1   | 0                  | 0                   | 1              | (10, 13)                                             | 0
2   | 0                  | 6                   | 0              | (10, 5)                                              | 6
3   | 6                  | 10                  | 0              | (6, 5)                                               | 4
4   | 10                 | 10                  | 1              | (0, 5)                                               | 0

Thus, all five cars are served, and the maximum waiting time is 6.

To serve all five cars, dispenser 0 must serve the cars with demands 6, 4, and 6, while dispenser 1 must serve the cars with demands 8 and 5. Therefore, car 2 must wait until time 6 for dispenser 0 to become free, so no assignment serving all five cars can have a maximum waiting time less than 6.

Example 2:

Input: demand = [10,15], fuel = [12,17]
Output: 0
Explanation:
- At time 0, Car 0 becomes allowed and starts refuelling using dispenser 0.
- Car 1 becomes allowed at time 0 (when Car 0 starts) and immediately starts refuelling using dispenser 1.
- Both cars start without waiting, so the maximum waiting time is 0.

Example 3:

Input: demand = [10,5], fuel = [8,8]
Output: -1
Explanation:
- At time 0, Car 0 becomes allowed. However, neither dispenser has enough fuel to serve it, so the process terminates immediately.
- No car is served, so the answer is -1.

Constraints:

    1 <= demand.length <= 50
    1 <= demand[i] <= 20
    fuel.length == 2
    1 <= fuel[i] <= 50
"""


class Solution:
    def minMaxWaitingTime(self, demand: List[int], fuel: List[int]) -> int:
        n = len(demand)

        # Check how many cars can be served with given max waiting time limit
        def can_serve(max_wait: int) -> bool:
            # dp[i][f0][f1] = earliest time dispenser 0 and 1 are free after serving i cars with f0, f1 fuel left
            # But this is too large for fuel up to 50 and n up to 50.
            # Instead, we use a BFS or DFS with memoization on (index, fuel0, fuel1, free0, free1)
            # But free0 and free1 can be large (up to sum of demands).
            # We can do a DFS with pruning and memoization.

            from functools import lru_cache

            @lru_cache(None)
            def dfs(i: int, f0: int, f1: int, free0: int, free1: int) -> bool:
                if i == n:
                    return True
                d = demand[i]
                allowed_time = 0 if i == 0 else start_times[i - 1]
                # Car i becomes allowed at start_times[i-1]
                # We try to assign dispenser 0 or 1 if possible

                # Wait time = start_time - allowed_time <= max_wait
                # start_time >= allowed_time
                # start_time >= free dispenser time
                # start_time = max(allowed_time, free dispenser time)
                # waiting_time = start_time - allowed_time

                # Try dispenser 0
                if f0 >= d:
                    start_time = max(allowed_time, free0)
                    wait_time = start_time - allowed_time
                    if wait_time <= max_wait:
                        # Update start_times[i] for next car
                        start_times[i] = start_time
                        if dfs(i + 1, f0 - d, f1, start_time + d, free1):
                            return True

                # Try dispenser 1
                if f1 >= d:
                    start_time = max(allowed_time, free1)
                    wait_time = start_time - allowed_time
                    if wait_time <= max_wait:
                        start_times[i] = start_time
                        if dfs(i + 1, f0, f1 - d, free0, start_time + d):
                            return True

                return False

            # We need to know start_times for allowed times
            # But start_times depends on assignment, so we try to simulate with a list
            # We'll store start_times in a list and update during recursion
            # Initialize start_times with zeros
            start_times.clear()
            start_times.extend([0] * n)
            return dfs(0, fuel[0], fuel[1], 0, 0)

        # First, find max number of cars that can be served ignoring waiting time
        # We can do a greedy approach to find max served cars:
        # Since cars must be served in order, and each car must be assigned to a dispenser with enough fuel,
        # we can try all possible assignments with backtracking to find max served cars.
        # But this is expensive.

        # Instead, we can do binary search on number of cars served:
        # For k in [0..n], check if we can serve first k cars with any assignment ignoring waiting time.
        # Then for that k, binary search on max waiting time.

        # Check if can serve first k cars ignoring waiting time
        def can_serve_k(k: int) -> bool:
            # DP with memoization on (index, fuel0, fuel1)
            from functools import lru_cache

            @lru_cache(None)
            def dfs_k(i: int, f0: int, f1: int) -> bool:
                if i == k:
                    return True
                d = demand[i]
                res = False
                if f0 >= d:
                    res = dfs_k(i + 1, f0 - d, f1)
                if not res and f1 >= d:
                    res = dfs_k(i + 1, f0, f1 - d)
                return res

            return dfs_k(0, fuel[0], fuel[1])

        # Binary search max number of cars served
        left, right = 0, n
        max_served = 0
        while left <= right:
            mid = (left + right) // 2
            if can_serve_k(mid):
                max_served = mid
                left = mid + 1
            else:
                right = mid - 1

        if max_served == 0:
            return -1

        # Now binary search on max waiting time for max_served cars
        start_times = []

        left, right = 0, sum(demand)
        ans = -1
        while left <= right:
            mid = (left + right) // 2
            if can_serve(mid):
                ans = mid
                right = mid - 1
            else:
                left = mid + 1

        return ans


sol = Solution()

print(sol.minMaxWaitingTime([6, 8, 4, 6, 5], [16, 13]))  # 6

assert sol.minMaxWaitingTime([6, 8, 4, 6, 5], [16, 13]) == 6
assert sol.minMaxWaitingTime([10, 15], [12, 17]) == 0
assert sol.minMaxWaitingTime([10, 5], [8, 8]) == -1

assert sol.minMaxWaitingTime([1], [1, 1]) == 0
assert sol.minMaxWaitingTime([20] * 50, [50, 50]) == -1
assert sol.minMaxWaitingTime([5, 5, 5, 5, 5], [10, 10]) == -1
assert sol.minMaxWaitingTime([10, 10, 10, 10, 10], [50, 0]) == 10
assert sol.minMaxWaitingTime([10, 10, 10, 10, 10], [0, 50]) == 10
assert sol.minMaxWaitingTime([1, 2, 3, 4, 5], [5, 5]) == -1
assert sol.minMaxWaitingTime([20, 1, 20, 1, 20], [40, 20]) == -1
assert sol.minMaxWaitingTime([20, 20, 20, 20, 20], [50, 49]) == -1
assert sol.minMaxWaitingTime([1] * 50, [50, 50]) == 1
assert sol.minMaxWaitingTime([20, 19, 18, 17, 16], [50, 50]) == -1
assert sol.minMaxWaitingTime([10] * 25 + [20] * 25, [500, 500]) == 10
assert sol.minMaxWaitingTime([20] * 50, [1, 1]) == -1
